scope: Theorem 4.1 (Rapid decay with alternating memories) of the manuscript “Computation under Rapidly Vanishing Navier–Stokes Forcing” (preprints/Computation-under-Rapidly-Vanishing-Navier-Stokes-Forcing-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 931c07840228968b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive computable viscosity. From a deterministic Turing machine and a finite input one can effectively construct a smooth force f on [0, ∞) × R3, with spatial support contained in a fixed compact set independent of time, such that for every J, l ≥ 0 and spatial multi-index α, sup t≥0, X∈R3 (1 + t + |X|)J |∂l t∂α Xf(t, X)| < ∞. (26) The solution with zero initial velocity is explicit, global, and unique in the class (2), with pressure zero. Its velocity satisfies the same support and derivative estimates. The material particle initially at (−1, 0, 0) reaches X1 > 0 if and only if the machine halts.
